input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The separator selection negates any_prefix_is_slash, picking ' / ' exactly when an option spelling already starts with a slash and '; ' otherwise.
- failure path: An option declared as --shout/--no-shout renders in --help as '--shout; --no-shout', and a Windows-style /debug;/no-debug option renders as '/debug / /no-debug', where the slash separator is indistinguishable from the slash prefix of the names.

Reviewer finding
- description: The separator selection in get_help_spec is inverted relative to the original code. The original used "; " when any_prefix_is_slash was true and " / " otherwise. The new code uses "; " when the flag is false and " / " when it is true.
- rationale: Trigger: any option whose prefixes are rendered with slashes, such as a boolean flag "--shout/--no-shout" (any_prefix_is_slash is true), and any option without slash prefixes (flag false). For the slash case the joiner becomes " / " where it used to be "; ", and for the normal case it becomes "; " where it used to be " / ". Because get_help_record now returns get_help_spec(ctx), every help record's left column is affected. The help output shows the wrong separator for every option, which is a visible regression in the rendered --help text.
critique: The finding identifies the same defect: the separator choice on any_prefix_is_slash is inverted, so slash-prefixed options get ' / ' and normal options get '; '. Its example wrongly treats --shout/--no-shout as slash-prefixed, but the faulty operation and the way it goes wrong match the label.
